decision: Where should the API's rate-limit counters live?
context: The API runs on 12 instances across 3 regions. Redis is already deployed in every region with 99.95% uptime. Limits must hold across instances within one second.

options.name: redis
options.text: Redis INCR with a TTL per key

options.name: memory
options.text: An in-process LRU cache on each instance

options.name: postgres
options.text: A counters table in the main Postgres database

options.name: edge
options.text: Rate-limit rules at the CDN edge

decision: What should run background jobs?
context: Jobs are email sends and PDF renders, about 2,000 per hour. The team already runs Postgres and has no Kafka or RabbitMQ. Jobs must survive a deploy.

options.name: pgqueue
options.text: A Postgres-backed queue using SKIP LOCKED

options.name: kafka
options.text: A new Kafka cluster

options.name: cron
options.text: A cron job that polls a table every minute

options.name: inprocess
options.text: An in-process worker pool inside the web servers

decision: How should the single-page app keep users signed in?
context: The single-page app and its API share one domain. Logout must take effect immediately. There is no mobile client.

options.name: cookie
options.text: An HttpOnly session cookie backed by a server-side session store

options.name: jwtlocal
options.text: A JWT in localStorage with a 24-hour expiry

options.name: jwtcookie
options.text: A JWT in an HttpOnly cookie with a 24-hour expiry and no revocation list

options.name: basic
options.text: HTTP basic auth on every request

decision: Where should user uploads be stored?
context: Users upload images up to 20 MB, about 50 GB per month. The app runs on stateless containers that are replaced on every deploy. A CDN is already in front of the app.

options.name: objectstore
options.text: S3-compatible object storage served through the CDN

options.name: localdisk
options.text: The container's local disk

options.name: database
options.text: A BLOB column in Postgres

options.name: nfs
options.text: A shared NFS volume mounted into every container

decision: How should the web service be deployed?
context: A stateless web service runs 6 replicas behind a load balancer. Database migrations are backward compatible. Downtime is not acceptable during business hours.

options.name: rolling
options.text: A rolling update, one replica at a time

options.name: recreate
options.text: Stop every replica, then start the new version

options.name: bluegreen
options.text: A full blue/green switch at the load balancer

options.name: manual
options.text: SSH into each host and restart it by hand

decision: How should the payment client be tested in CI?
context: The client calls a third-party payment API whose sandbox allows 5 requests per minute. CI runs on every pull request, about 40 times a day.

options.name: mocks
options.text: Unit tests against recorded fixtures of the API's responses

options.name: sandboxci
options.text: Call the sandbox from every CI run

options.name: prodtests
options.text: Run the tests against production with small amounts

options.name: none
options.text: No automated tests; manual QA before each release

decision: What format should the services log in?
context: Logs go to a platform that indexes JSON fields. On-call engineers search by request id and user id. Log volume is 30 GB a day.

options.name: json
options.text: Structured JSON lines with request_id and user_id fields

options.name: text
options.text: Plain text lines

options.name: csv
options.text: CSV lines

options.name: debugall
options.text: Plain text at debug level everywhere

decision: How should feature flags be managed?
context: The team ships daily and wants to turn features off without a deploy. There are 3 services in 2 languages. A budget for a vendor is approved.

options.name: vendor
options.text: A hosted feature-flag service with SDKs for both languages

options.name: envvars
options.text: Environment variables read at startup

options.name: configfile
options.text: A JSON file in the repository

options.name: dbtable
options.text: A flags table that each service polls every 10 minutes

decision: How should catalog search work?
context: The catalog has 40,000 items. Users need typo-tolerant search and filters by category and price. The team runs Postgres and no search engine today.

options.name: pgtrgm
options.text: Postgres full-text search with pg_trgm

options.name: elastic
options.text: A new Elasticsearch cluster

options.name: like
options.text: SQL LIKE queries

options.name: client
options.text: Load every item into the browser and filter there

decision: How should product pages be cached?
context: Product pages change a few times a day and are identical for all anonymous users. 90% of traffic is anonymous. The site is behind a CDN.

options.name: cdn
options.text: Cache anonymous pages at the CDN with a 5-minute TTL and purge on update

options.name: redis
options.text: Cache rendered HTML in Redis

options.name: nocache
options.text: Render every request

options.name: browser
options.text: Cache-Control max-age of one week in the browser

decision: Where should service secrets live?
context: Services run on Kubernetes in one cloud account. Secrets must be rotated every 90 days and every access must be audited.

options.name: cloudsm
options.text: The cloud provider's secret manager with rotation and audit logs

options.name: kubesecrets
options.text: Plain Kubernetes Secrets edited by hand

options.name: envfile
options.text: A .env file committed to the repository, encrypted with a shared key

options.name: wiki
options.text: The team wiki

decision: How should the breaking change to the public API ship?
context: A public REST API has 300 external integrators. A breaking change to the orders endpoint is needed. Integrators need at least 6 months of notice.

options.name: urlversion
options.text: A /v2 path that runs alongside /v1 for 6 months

options.name: inplace
options.text: Change /v1 in place and email the integrators

options.name: header
options.text: Version by a custom header, with v1 as the default

options.name: newapi
options.text: A new GraphQL API that replaces REST

decision: How should the NOT NULL column be added?
context: A Postgres table has 200 million rows and a column must become NOT NULL with a default. Writes happen continuously, and locks longer than a few seconds cause user errors.

options.name: batched
options.text: Add a nullable column, backfill in batches, then add the constraint as NOT VALID and validate it

options.name: single
options.text: One ALTER TABLE with the default and NOT NULL

options.name: dumprestore
options.text: Dump, transform and restore during a maintenance window

options.name: app
options.text: Handle nulls in application code forever

decision: What should page the on-call engineer?
context: On-call gets paged at night. Most current alerts fire on CPU above 80% and are ignored. The service has a 99.9% availability SLO.

options.name: slo
options.text: Alert on the burn rate of the error and latency SLO

options.name: cpu
options.text: Keep the CPU alerts and lower the threshold to 70%

options.name: everything
options.text: Page on every error log line

options.name: none
options.text: No pages; check dashboards in the morning

decision: How should the field app sync offline changes?
context: A field-service mobile app must work without signal for hours. Two technicians rarely edit the same job. Conflicts must never lose data silently.

options.name: queuelww
options.text: A local queue of changes, synced on reconnect, last-write-wins per field with a conflict log

options.name: onlineonly
options.text: Require a connection for every action

options.name: fullreplace
options.text: Upload the whole local database and overwrite the server copy

options.name: crdt
options.text: A full CRDT framework for every model

decision: How should the app send email?
context: The app sends password resets and receipts, about 10,000 emails a day. Deliverability matters and the team has no email infrastructure. Bounces must be tracked.

options.name: provider
options.text: A transactional email provider with bounce webhooks

options.name: ownsmtp
options.text: Run our own SMTP server

options.name: gmail
options.text: A shared Gmail account over SMTP

options.name: sendbatch
options.text: Send everything once a day in one batch

decision: How should the four services' code be organised?
context: Four services share TypeScript types and release together every week. Six engineers work across all of them. CI takes 8 minutes per repository today.

options.name: monorepo
options.text: One repository with workspaces and CI that runs only what changed

options.name: polyrepo
options.text: Keep four repositories and publish the shared types as a package

options.name: copy
options.text: Copy the shared types into each repository by hand

options.name: submodules
options.text: Git submodules for the shared code

decision: How should photo thumbnails be produced?
context: Uploaded photos need 3 thumbnail sizes. Uploads peak at 50 per minute. The CDN supports on-the-fly image transforms with caching.

options.name: cdntransform
options.text: CDN image transforms with cached variants

options.name: worker
options.text: A background worker that resizes on upload

options.name: request
options.text: Resize inside the web request before responding

options.name: client
options.text: Resize in the browser before upload, nowhere else

decision: How should per-environment configuration work?
context: The service runs in dev, staging and production. Values differ per environment and a few are secrets. Deploys use the same container image everywhere.

options.name: envconfig
options.text: Environment variables per environment, with secrets from the secret manager

options.name: images
options.text: Build a different image per environment

options.name: branch
options.text: A git branch per environment with its own config

options.name: hardcode
options.text: Hard-code the values behind if statements on the hostname

decision: How should calls to the inventory API handle failures?
context: The downstream inventory API fails about 2% of requests with a 503 and recovers within seconds. Calls are idempotent reads. The user-facing latency budget is 2 seconds.

options.name: backoff
options.text: Retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff and jitter inside the 2-second budget

options.name: infinite
options.text: Retry until it succeeds

options.name: noretry
options.text: Fail the user request on the first error

options.name: fixed
options.text: Retry 10 times, every 100 ms
